aggregation.reason: No default. These are different time points, and averaging them destroys the signal — the change over time IS the signal. Which summary replaces it comes from your research question, not from the data.

findings.title: `pid` repeats across rows.
findings.detail: `pid` has `600` values across `3,209` rows, about 5.3 rows each and at most `6`. Rows of one participant share everything about it.
findings.why_it_matters: A split that puts one participant's rows on both sides lets a model recognize people instead of learning, and every score looks better than it is. As the identifier, it keeps each participant's rows together.

findings.title: Which of these is the event you are predicting?
findings.detail: `cvd` is the outcome and holds two values — '0' (3,145 rows) and '1' (64 rows).

Nothing in the file says which one you are predicting. By convention '1' is usually the event, and it is the smaller group here — but convention is a suggestion, not an answer.

exposure_forms.label: Restricted cubic spline
exposure_forms.customary: Increasingly customary in nutritional epidemiology: "now near-default" (NUTRITION_PACK §07G; Desquilbet & Mariotti 2010).
exposure_forms.sound: Sound: a smooth curve with few parameters, linear in the tails, with a test of nonlinearity; knots at Harrell's percentiles of the fitting rows.
exposure_forms.consequence: Adds a curve's terms per exposure and a test of whether it bends.

exposure_forms.label: Straight line
exposure_forms.customary: Customary: one coefficient per unit of intake.
exposure_forms.sound: Sound when the relation is close to a line; a curve it misses biases the slope.
exposure_forms.consequence: One coefficient per unit; no curvature.

exposure_forms.label: Quintiles with a trend test
exposure_forms.customary: Customary in nutritional epidemiology: "quintiles remain expected alongside" the spline (NUTRITION_PACK §07G).
exposure_forms.sound: Weak for prediction: five steps discard the variation within each fifth.
exposure_forms.consequence: Four indicators against the lowest fifth, and a trend across medians.

methods.label: Multiple imputation (m at least 20, more when more rows are incomplete)
methods.customary: Customary in epidemiology (Sterne et al. 2009, BMJ 338:b2393)
methods.sound: Sound: with the outcome and energy in the imputation model it is unbiased under missing at random and its intervals carry the imputation's uncertainty (Moons et al. 2006).

methods.label: Complete cases
methods.customary: Customary in epidemiology; most software's default
methods.sound: Sound if complete cases give unbiased coefficients only if whether a value is missing does not depend on the outcome, given the predictors (Groenwold et al. 2012; White & Carlin 2010); it costs every incomplete row.

methods.label: Single fill in each training fold
methods.sound: Unsound for an interval: a single fill treats each imputed value as measured, so the intervals are too narrow, and a median fill biases a coefficient whenever who is missing depends on another variable.

methods.label: Single fill with missing indicators
methods.customary: Customary in prediction from health records (Sperrin et al. 2020)
methods.sound: Unsound for an estimate: the missing-indicator method almost always biases the estimates of a nonrandomized study (Groenwold et al. 2012); it is valid for baseline covariates in a randomized trial.

methods.label: Blanks as their own level
methods.customary: Customary for questions not asked (a blank medication answer)
methods.sound: The missing-indicator method for categories: the missing-indicator method almost always biases the estimates of a nonrandomized study (Groenwold et al. 2012); it is valid for baseline covariates in a randomized trial; sound when a blank means not asked (then it is a value, not missing).

below_detection.label: Censoring-aware
below_detection.customary: Less common in metabolomics; the epidemiology of exposures below detection (Lubin et al. 2004)
below_detection.sound: Sound for associations. A censored-normal (Tobit) draw below the limit within the multiple imputation, given the outcome (Lubin et al. 2004).

below_detection.label: Half the smallest detected value

below_detection.label: As any other blank (the median fill)

imputation_models.customary: Chained equations with derived terms made in each copy (passive) are the field's habit (mice's and Stata's defaults)
imputation_models.sound: Sound: SMC-FCS where the model holds a spline, a log, a ratio or a logistic or Cox outcome, chained equations where it is linear in the imputed values (Bartlett et al. 2015)

imputation_models.label: Passive: terms derived in each completed copy
imputation_models.customary: Customary: mice's and Stata's ice defaults derive transformed and product terms in each completed copy
imputation_models.sound: Unsound with a declared nonlinear term: passive imputation draws each value from a model linear in it and only then derives the declared nonlinear terms, so the curvature and the nonlinearity tests would be biased toward the null (Bartlett et al. 2015)

imputation_models.label: Single-level on clustered rows
imputation_models.customary: Customary: chained equations that ignore the clustering
imputation_models.sound: Unsound on clustered rows: imputing clustered rows one at a time gives a unit's time-invariant values different draws on its different rows and erases the correlation within units (Lüdtke, Robitzsch & Grund 2017)

missing.tension: Complete cases are the field's habit; when the blanks depend on measured variables they may be biased, and multiple imputation with the outcome is sounder (Sterne et al. 2009, BMJ 338:b2393).

exposure_forms.label: Restricted cubic spline
exposure_forms.customary: Increasingly customary in nutritional epidemiology: "now near-default" (NUTRITION_PACK §07G; Desquilbet & Mariotti 2010).
exposure_forms.sound: Sound: a smooth curve with few parameters, linear in the tails, with a test of nonlinearity; knots at Harrell's percentiles of the fitting rows.
exposure_forms.consequence: Adds a curve's terms per exposure and a test of whether it bends.

exposure_forms.label: Straight line
exposure_forms.customary: Customary: one coefficient per unit of intake.

exposure_forms.label: Quintiles with a trend test
exposure_forms.customary: Customary in nutritional epidemiology: "quintiles remain expected alongside" the spline (NUTRITION_PACK §07G).
exposure_forms.sound: Weaker for inference: cutting a continuous intake into fifths discards the variation within each fifth and assumes a step at each cut; the trend test scores each fifth by its median.
exposure_forms.consequence: Four indicators against the lowest fifth, and a trend across medians.

floor.text: A held-out score needs at least 100 events and 100 non-events to be estimated with useful precision.
floor.source: Collins, Ogundimu & Altman, Stat Med 2016;35:214–226; Vergouwe et al., J Clin Epidemiol 2005;58:475–483

options.label: Cross-validation only
options.measures: Every row trains and is scored by cross-validation; no untouched final score.

options.label: Hold out 10%
options.measures: About `321` held-out rows, `6` in the rarer class: AUC known to about ±0.23.

options.label: Hold out 20%
options.measures: About `642` held-out rows, `13` in the rarer class: AUC known to about ±0.15.

options.label: Hold out 30%
options.measures: About `963` held-out rows, `19` in the rarer class: AUC known to about ±0.13.

base.reason: Of `3,209` rows analyzed, a 20% holdout leaves about `13` held-out rows in the rarer class, below the floor of 100 events and 100 non-events; cross-validation reuses every row, so it comes first.
base.precision_note: Widths are approximate 95% intervals of a score on that many held-out rows: R² by its large-sample standard error 2·√R²·(1 − R²)/√n at an R² of 0.2, AUC by Hanley & McNeil (1982) at an AUC of 0.75, macro-F1 by a proportion's interval on the rarest class.
base.refusal: The held-out rows are drawn by the grain answer: say first whether a unit can appear in more than one row.

options.label: Bootstrap optimism correction
options.measures: Every row trains and scores; 500 whole-pipeline refits on resamples estimate the optimism.
options.cost: about 500 refits of each family, besides 50 for the comparisons' 10 × 5-fold repeats
options.caution: Sound for regression-type families; a near-interpolating one (boosted trees) keeps its cross-validated score, since the bootstrap overstates it (Coley et al. 2023).

options.label: Repeated cross-validation (10 × 5)
options.measures: The folds are drawn 10 times, so the score no longer rests on one partition.

options.label: Cross-validation, once
options.measures: One partition into folds: cheap, and noisier at small sizes.
options.cost: 50 refits of each family: the score's 5-fold run is the first of the comparisons' 10 × 5-fold repeats

options.label: Internal–external, by cluster
options.measures: Each site, study or period scored by models fit on the others, with the spread.
options.cost: one refit of each family per cluster, besides 50 for the comparisons' 10 × 5-fold repeats

validation.reason: With 3,209 rows, below about 20,000, one split or one partition gives an unstable score (Harrell); resampling the whole pipeline uses every row, so it comes first.
validation.holdout_note: A holdout is a lockbox against analyst overfitting; at 3,209 rows it costs precision: its rows neither train the models nor enter the resampled score.
validation.source: Harrell 2017, Split-sample model validation: data splitting is unstable below about 20,000 subjects

sound.reason: Draws the folds several times, so the score no longer rests on one partition.

patches.methods: The effect of `dash` on `cvd` was estimated by a marginal structural model with stabilized inverse-probability weights (Robins, Hernán & Brumback 2000). The weights came from pooled logistic models of `dash` at each of 6 time points, given its previous value, `female`, `age` and time and its square (numerator) and also `sbp` (denominator). The outcome model was a weighted pooled logistic model of `cvd` on the number of time points exposed so far, `female`, `age` and time and its square, with a CR2 variance clustered by `pid` and Bell–McCaffrey degrees of freedom (Bell & McCaffrey 2002) that treats the weights as known, so its interval is conservative (Hernán, Brumback & Robins 2000). No loss-to-follow-up indicator was declared: 63 units' rows end before the last time point without the event, and the estimate assumes their loss is unrelated to the outcome. `sbp` is a time-varying confounder affected by prior `dash`, which standard regression cannot adjust for. The truncation is declared after the weights' distribution and positivity at each time point are read; no estimate is computed before it. The estimate assumes no unmeasured confounding at each time point given the history, positivity, and that each time point's `dash` precedes the outcome it is paired with, as declared.

The outcome model was a weighted pooled logistic model of `cvd` on the number of time points exposed so far, `female`, `age` and time and its square, with a CR2 variance clustered by `pid` and Bell–McCaffrey degrees of freedom (Bell & McCaffrey 2002) that treats the weights as known, so its interval is conservative (Hernán, Brumback & Robins 2000). base.se_definition: Each standard error counts which rows were scored, with each fold's model as fitted (LeDell et al. 2015; DeLong's for the AUC); it leaves out how the models would vary with other training rows.

No resampling (SMOTE, over- or undersampling) or class weighting was applied: customary in machine-learning papers, resampling overestimates the rarer class's probability without raising the AUC (van den Goorbergh et al. 2022); a decision moves the threshold instead.

estimand.caption: The total effect of `dash` on `cvd`, as a conditional odds ratio per unit of `dash`, conditional on `female` and `age`; `sbp` left out as a consequence of the exposure; a conditional ratio, which changes with the covariates even without confounding (the adjustment set by the disjunctive cause criterion, VanderWeele 2019, Eur J Epidemiol 34:211–219).
estimand.time_varying: The estimate of `dash` is the time-varying lane's (a marginal structural model with stabilized inverse-probability weights). This model cannot adjust for `sbp`, a confounder affected by prior `dash`, so its row for `dash` is not the effect.

base.tension: AUC is the customary headline: it ranks risks without asking whether they are right (semi-proper), so the models were compared, chosen and declared on log loss, a strictly proper score (Van Calster et al., STRATOS TG6).

diagnostics.method: Leverage and Cook's distance of every row, as R's hatvalues and cooks.distance give them, against the median of F(4, 3,205) = 0.839 (Cook 1977, Technometrics 19:15)

base.methods: The estimate of `dash` is reported across a declared sequence of models fit on all 3,209 analyzed rows: unadjusted; Model 2, the primary, adjusted for `female` and `age`. Only the exposure's estimates are shown as effects; every other coefficient is listed apart as an adjustment term, not an effect estimate (Westreich & Greenland 2013, Am J Epidemiol 177:292). Influence was checked by Cook's distance against the median of F(4, 3,205) (Cook 1977, Technometrics 19:15): 0 rows above it. Sensitivity to unmeasured confounding is reported by the E-value for the estimate and for the confidence limit nearer the null, never as a pass or a fail.

342bae81ade143c0932016dbec72d9e7.sentence: The table was read through the `clinical` lens.

4daae555da6445a6801fc67e4017082d.sentence: `cvd` was chosen as the outcome; it is measured on all `3,209` rows.

d956ec85b23d4d91b8f37e3fe6802c8c.sentence: `1` of `cvd` was taken as the event and coded 1; `0` was coded 0.

bbd0838bcca24e2aa6345f382ff004ea.sentence: `cvd` was analyzed as a yes/no outcome: everyone was followed for the same time, as answered, so it counts events over one period.

d6077d8a0d0e42edb89a1c4621ae8479.sentence: The analysis was declared for `inference`: associations are estimated with their uncertainty.

57d5446f1ac94e0e9f8c3687c123dc43.sentence: Participants were declared to appear in more than one row, identified by `pid`: `3,209` rows from `600` of them, at most `6` each.

3ee43d0d2bce4fde9e2bc4eef7056f80.sentence: Each `pid`'s rows were taken as different time points, ordered by `visit`.

48f37bfe765243098db20cc8d108a89c.sentence: The analysis was kept at one row per record; each `pid`'s rows stay together on one side of the split.

99e15b7088654c7a845cc5103037e744.sentence: The model was declared not to predict forward in time: rows are held out at random, with each `pid`'s rows kept together.

de5f6634b8674f7e9e3df4e4f5c1ee0e.sentence: Column roles were set for `7` columns: exposure `dash`; covariates `sbp`, `female` and `age`; identifier `pid`; time column `visit`; excluded `lost`; `visit`, `dash` and `sbp` were proposed below high confidence and wait for their own confirmation before any default reads them.

a31ea8d0042643f087a22915a855e71d.sentence: Confirmed together, each as the question showed it: `visit` was confirmed as a time column; `dash` was confirmed as an exposure; `sbp` was confirmed as a covariate.

e48abfd94e3949ed9bae75c0ce25a6c5.sentence: No rows were excluded: every row with `cvd` measured stays in the analysis.
